findings.heading: Building a UI
findings.proposition: The English names the generic column panel function as column(); the Turkish names it sutun() (sütun()), which is not a shiny function.
findings.reader_consequence: A Turkish reader writing sütun() in a fluidPage layout gets 'could not find function' and cannot build a column panel.

findings.heading: Building a UI
findings.proposition: The English gives plotOutput() as the example of an xxxOutput() function; the Turkish gives plotCikis() (plotÇıkış()), which is not a shiny function and contradicts the UI chunk below that uses plotOutput("malaria_epicurve").
findings.reader_consequence: A Turkish reader learns a non-existent output function name and cannot connect renderPlot() in the server to the UI.

findings.heading: Developing an app server
findings.proposition: The English says the epicurve output has the outputId malaria_epicurve, matching plotOutput("malaria_epicurve") in the chunk above; the Turkish says the outputId is sitma_epicurve (sıtma_epicurve), which appears nowhere in the code.
findings.reader_consequence: The very next paragraph tells the reader the names must match exactly between ui and server, so a reader following the Turkish uses output$sitma_epicurve and the plot never renders.

findings.heading: Loading data into our app
findings.proposition: The English says the district INPUT could arrive as a character vector with multiple values, which is why %in% is used; the Turkish says the %in% OPERATOR can be used as a character vector with multiple values.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader loses the actual reason for %in% (multi-select widgets return a vector) and is told something false about the operator itself, so they may keep == in their own filters.

findings.heading: Loading data into our app
findings.proposition: The English says to create a new FILE called global.R inside your app's directory; the Turkish attaches the name global.R to the DIRECTORY ('Uygulamanizin global.R adli dizininde yeni bir dosya olusturun').
findings.reader_consequence: A reader creates a folder named global.R and puts an arbitrarily named file in it, so shiny never runs the startup code and the app fails with objects not found.

findings.heading: Loading data into our app
findings.proposition: The English attributes the automatic recognition of app.R, server.R, ui.R and global.R to shiny; the Turkish attributes it to 'Bright', a package that does not exist.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader is told a non-existent package provides the file-name convention and cannot search for or verify the behaviour.

findings.heading: Sharing shiny apps
findings.proposition: The English names shinyapps.io as the recommended hosting service; the Turkish names brightapps.io, which is not the shiny hosting service.
findings.reader_consequence: A reader trying to publish their app goes to a wrong or non-existent domain and cannot create the account the section then tells them to create.

findings.heading: Recommended extension packages
findings.proposition: The English names the extra-widgets package as shinyWidgets; the first Turkish bullet names it brightWidgets, while the same bullet still tells the reader to run shinyWidgets::shinyWidgetsGallery().
findings.reader_consequence: A reader tries to install a package called brightWidgets, which does not exist on CRAN, and is left with a bullet that contradicts its own code line.

findings.heading: Recommended extension packages
findings.proposition: The English lists the recommended extension packages once; the Turkish repeats the entire list twice (shinyWidgets, shinyjs, shinydashboard, shinydashboardPlus, shinythemes, then the DT and plotly paragraph), first at lines 1393-1408 and again at lines 1410-1424, with the second copy leaving the shinyWidgets bullet untranslated in English.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader sees every recommendation twice with differing details (the first copy has no hyperlinks for shinyjs, shinydashboard, shinydashboardPlus or shinythemes, the second copy does) and cannot tell which listing is authoritative.

findings.heading: Sharing shiny apps
findings.proposition: The English says the `here` package solves the explicit-file-path problem; the Turkish renders the package name as the ordinary word 'buradaki' ('the package here'), so no package is named.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader is told a package fixes hard-coded paths on a server but is never told which one, so their app keeps absolute paths and fails once deployed.

findings.heading: Before you start to build an app
findings.proposition: The English qualifies the claim as 'you can't really visualise what you're building UNLESS you are aiming for something specific'; the Turkish drops the conditional clause and states only that you cannot visualise what you are building.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader loses the actual advice of the paragraph, that having a specific target in mind is what makes the UI imaginable, and is left with a bare discouraging statement.

findings.heading: Building a UI
findings.proposition: The English says checkboxInput() passes a logical object, `TRUE` or `FALSE`; the Turkish gives the values as DOGRU or YANLIS (DOĞRU / YANLIŞ), which are not R logical literals.
findings.reader_consequence: A reader testing the widget value writes if (input$x == DOĞRU) and gets an 'object not found' error instead of a working condition.

findings.heading: Dashboards with Shiny
findings.proposition: The English links the alternative dashboard method to the flexdashboard chapter with a working markdown link; the Turkish keeps the bracketed label but removes the link target, so no destination is given.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader sees literal square brackets and cannot navigate to the R Markdown dashboards chapter that is being recommended.

findings.heading: Dashboards with Shiny
findings.proposition: The English says producing a dashboard WITH SHINY requires relatively advanced R knowledge; the Turkish says producing a QUALITY dashboard ('Kaliteli bir gosterge paneli') does, dropping the attribution to shiny.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader takes the difficulty warning as being about dashboard quality in general rather than about shiny specifically, and loses the contrast the page draws with the easier flexdashboard route.

findings.heading: Developing an app server
findings.proposition: The English says there IS an order (a sequence) to the server tasks; the Turkish says 'Onlara verilen bir emir vardir' ('there is a command given to them'), translating 'order' as an instruction rather than a sequence.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader loses the point that server tasks do have an execution ordering they need not yet understand, and instead reads an unrelated statement about commands.

findings.heading: Recommended resources
findings.proposition: The English has a final section heading '## Recommended resources'; the Turkish file has no counterpart heading.
findings.reader_consequence: The Turkish page ends without the Recommended resources section, so a reader following the two versions side by side finds no place where further resources are to be listed.

findings.heading: Sharing shiny apps
findings.proposition: The English carries the italic editorial placeholder '*signing up for account*' between the server-readiness paragraph and the token instructions; the Turkish omits it, while keeping the other placeholder at the end of the section.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader moves straight from server preparation to 'once you have your account' with no marker that the account sign-up step is undocumented.
